answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent, a cost that scales linearly for fakes but stays fixed for the honest. The verifier monitors the network as a dense grove of identities, rejecting any entry that reuses a prior output. While one honest agent pays the base fee, an attacker scaling 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a hard shale floor. Any duplicate bridge of logic triggers a burn.
